[b]The Counter-Manifesto
[sub][i]by Cui Fang[/i][/sub][/b]

I recently had the pleasure of meeting again with the talented Argo Lo Pilato at Citharo for the Fifth Conference of Discussions. When we came to meet, he introduced me to another talent, a certain Immacolata Terrasi, who then introduced me to Cirino Sferrazza. Together, these three men (along with Pio Graci, my greatest brother) paved the way for the triumph of the socialist revolution in Gythena and the beginning of their so-called "New Order" of socialism.

So tantalizing it is for us witnesses to the changes made in history that we come to enrich the names of those who have risen so far up from the masses to become the great men of the age. Yet, it is precisely in the socialist praxis that we understand that there are no great men and that in this world are the immense multitudes of commons, of ordinaries, of mundane workers and laborers of all walks of life, their names forgotten, and yet whose contributions move the weight of the world to this very day. It is in socialism that we understand that the truth must be sought from [i]histoire vue d'en bas et non d'en haut.[/i]

And so, it is with sharp disclaim that I must express my disapproval in the various institutions and frameworks that presently make up the Socialist Technate of Northern Kianzhou.

In our Conference of Discussions, and most especially in our statement of policies, we approved of various points that became the fundamental truths of the New Socialism. The Technate, however, is a deformation of these fundamental truths, a most malformed alteration that betrays the revolution it was meant to create so as to supremely elevate above the proletariat a new class of technocratic masters.

[list][sup]"[i]That deviations from the dictatorship of the proletariat constitute a betrayal of the revolution and sanction of fascistic class collaboration[/i].  [b]Point 3, Statement of Policies[/b]"[/sup][/list]

The Technate offers us a new priesthood, one in which its priests do not speak under the authority of God but under examinations and credentials. The form changes, yet the substance is the same. The new master has come, and the majority obeys.

In Astanir, where ethnic conflict marauded the country all over during the height of the Civil War, QASIC identified one of the most egregious failings in its political system that enabled such horrible tragedy: that of "best practices". We know now in this age that the world is being increasingly connected. Academia is generally written and spoken in Llyndorran, and for many individuals, progress is tied to urban expansion and grey infrastructure. Such standardization in the fields of development is that we've come to accept the existence of the "best practices" for society.

And yet, what exactly is the cost of these "best practices"?

We must never forget that the purpose of this revolution is the emancipation of all peoples, of all sectors, across all nations. The pursuit of best practices is, therefore, a social abomination, which yields the functions of society to the unfeeling and technocratic elite.

During the Astaniran Civil War, QASIC troops spoke at great length with the native Argossian tribesmen about the impact of these best practices. For this, we must focus our attention on the town of Kalan, situated over the great Astaniran Karst.

Kalan has a culturally significant site that is now protected by the People's Republic of Astanir called the Rice Terraces of Kalan, a natively-designed system constituted by hundreds upon hundreds of stone weirs that divert water to the terraces during the growing season, which may then be dismantled to allow fish migration, jointly enabling proper soil regulation without the need for a complex reservoir. According to the Argossians, they developed this system independently nearly half a millennium ago as a green alternative to protect their highland forests, which in their belief systems housed the [i]pauno[/i] or spirits of their departed loved ones and relatives. 

When Sanguinian forces first took control of the Karst and consequently Kalan, the Argossians at the town lamented at the construction of a dam near their village that would flood the surrounding region, notably Kalan's culturally significant rice terraces, and instead supplant them with downriver irrigation capable of generating much stronger rice yields.

The issue with best practices is its cultural imperialism. To the unfeeling technocrat, all of existence is purposed for rational governance; cultural significance is a worthy sacrifice if it means to ensure the rigorous pursuit of utilitarian happiness. Because native knowledge is often oral, traditional, spiritual, and embedded in practice rather than written in reports, technocratic experts are unable to view it as knowledge. 

This is the epistemic violence of technocracy, that local traditions are merely reduced to data points on a graph, analyzed, and then recalibrated into a universal solution that must be applied everywhere.

[list][sup]"[i]That the final goal of every dictatorship is a stateless, classless, and communist society, which must be done appropriately in accordance with the transitional model from bourgeois capitalism to socialism, whereupon the productive mechanisms of the state are seized by the workers[/i].  [b]Point 4, Statement of Policies[/b]"[/sup][/list]

Now therefore, we come to the second problem of technocracy. If the purpose of technocracy is to install a new master based on academic credentials, then we have created the new bourgeoisie, and with it, the new imperial state. This state is called the Technate.

Those who support the Technate believe in its salient principles of a "well-oiled, meritocratic and technocratic machine" led by these new masters. A state that preserves itself indefinitely, especially one ruled by an educated elite, is the antithesis of the stateless communist society, and is instead a chauvinistic, bureaucratic, collectivist hegemony. It is a state that prides itself on the hubris of its administrative and technical expertise without any atom of regard for revolutionary credentials.

In Argo Lo Pilato's [i]Socialist Praxis[/i], he writes that one possible error that socialist parties make is organizational error, and further elaborates on the concept of "revisionist organization", that is, a socialist organization that cares little for ideological orthodoxy and revolutionary fervor, who accepts members voraciously, as perhaps through the scores in national examinations, who is reformed not for the pursuit of the classless, communist society, but for to judge and adjudge the lessers of the state, "to disarm the vanguard of the revolution and lay it naked before the imperialist powers of the world."

And yet still the Technate commits worse heterodoxies, as in Chapter One, where it fully repudiates not just liberal bourgeois democracy, but democracy entirely. It claims that democracy "allows for fools to govern the lives of millions" and that it "permits for damnable systems of votes that can stew into rabid tribalism and partisan conflicts".

Such views, while superficially radical, are in fact a dogmatic overcorrection that abandons the masses entirely and disempowers the proletariat by placing them under permanent administration.

In our own system, we disdain bourgeois democracy but adhere to democratic centralism, enabling all sectors of society to engage in participatory planning and assessments to enable agency across the whole of society. The "dictatorship of the proletariat" must prioritize establishing a dictatorship for its own sake. The problem of the Technate is that it describes no revolutionary process whatsoever. It presents a fully-formed system to be implemented, but offers no theory of how to get there beyond vague references to "revolution." I will tell you now that the process shall come through fascistic imposition.

[list][sup]"[i]That the protracted people's war is the inevitable comrade of revolution and must be honorably prosecuted by the vanguard in close collaboration with the united front of the rural peasantry and the urban petite bourgeoisie.[/i]  [b]Point 5, Statement of Policies[/b]"[/sup][/list]

Before a man may call himself a socialist, he must first answer the question: Is he a citizen of his country or a citizen of the world? Those who answer rightly follow the global revolution and support revolutionary struggles all over. Those who answer wrongly trade liberation for pragmatic revisionism. In their own words, the Technate asserts that "autarky and protectionism is the only way to preserve the revolution indefinitely."

It is this partiality that freezes revolutions and paralyzes the transition between the socialist state and the communist society.

It is proper to disdain capitalism and its inherent contradictions with human existence, but it is improper to forcibly subdue it without any regard for the mass line. Autarky is manifest when a society is fully sufficient in all of its needs and all of its abilities, and is therefore indicative of the stateless, classless, and communist society. Therefore, autarky is the final stage in the transition from socialism to communism.

A state that imposes autarky upon its people contradicts itself by the very fact of its own imposition, for to impose protectionist policies and to close down markets is to signify the supremacy of the state itself over the communist struggle.

It is the policy of this Socialist International that markets remain free and operational, capable of passing resources between nations. In bourgeois states, free trade is good because it exacerbates the very evils of the capitalist system, through its merciless, neo-colonialist extraction of resources from poorer nations. However, free trade is also good between socialist-oriented market economies, as in Qianxun, Sanguivallis, Gythena, and Astanir, who act according to the needs of the people and do so in the understanding of a headlong process of struggle towards true autarky state dissolution.

[list][sup]"[i]In such a nation where there is no revolutionary struggle, it is the duty of these member states to instigate one.[/i]  [b]Rakon Gilon[/b]"[/sup][/list]

This is a warning to all students of socialism.

If suppose you've come across a resident of the Socialist Technate and have studied their national texts and now believe that the time has come for this Socialist International to welcome its newest member, beware, for you've been misguided. Authority over socialism must come from orthodoxy and orthopraxy, from the mass line and the revolutionary struggle, from the vanguard party and its ideology, none of which the Technate sufficiently inculcates within its misguided, techno-fascist political framework.

No greater power is capable of usurping the workers of the world. Always remember that you have nothing to lose but your chains.

[/spoiler]

[b]Valid threat.[/b]

[i]The Salvation government has now apparently threatened the encroaching Emergency government forces by using nuclear artillery shells. The validity of their claim is under debate, but their usage of white phosphorous has made it clear that they might have some modicum of truth to their claim.[/i]

[spoiler=Cieskhalia Expansion (537 Words)][i]History,[/i] A man bellowed from the front of a university classroom. He wore a tweed jacket, a vest, and a button down. He pulled his tie loose during an impassioned lecture to some students on Shuskan Preservation- a movement gaining popularity in places like Cieskahlia and abroad. The man was a guest speaker, and part of a national tour of Cieskahlias four states- a propaganda campaign to make Koranvistani acquisition a popular thing.

Cieskhalia's people groups include the Krotsie in the north and Yalots in the south, with ethnic Francines on the Besson Islands and Beastmen (Typically Vulpid and Felid type) throughout the territories. They arrived to the area during the last wave of Shuskan Slavic Migrations that settled early Kyraniya and the area of the strait at Lake Elseyr's mouth. From there, the regional slavs adapted to a seafaring life and were subject to changes in broader regional power until their independence in 1833.

Krodtzen, the northernmost state, first approached the idea as a way to maintain peace in the region. Vasiliy, a northern coastal state in possession of the two [i]Îles Bessons[/i] and half of Tereyagretz (Terre yvi Graza/T.Gz). The other half of Terevogradza is under the control of the Black State of Iridigawzhia Klezmonov- a military state threatening an armed takeover of the rest of the T.Gz demilitarized zone over the alleged mistreatment of the several beastmen minorities on the northern half of the island.
The southernmost state is Yalokhagrad Metza, the last outpost of the Yalokuts Democratic Peoples Republic that collapsed in 2019.

The Yalokuts state had ruled since the 1925 socialist revolution, which brought about the DPR of Unitied Cieskhalia. Due to a lack of international support and external pressure from the EDU to adopt a capitalist democracy, the state was subject to constant factional infighting. In 2018, the state of Krodtzen declared independence with the support of the Llyndorran leadership and military, starting the downfall of the DPRUC. Milano Krazciec, the DPRUC Chair, resigned shortly after and dissolved the High Office, leading to a factional war in the Southern Territories for control. The Cieskah Civil War did extensive damage to the infrastructure in the south, and a ceasefire was put in place during August of 2022, and held until April of 2028.

The Black State Militia first faced off against the Vasiliy National Guard for control of the Island on April second, and fighting raged on for 14 days. The Three State Council, an uneasy body formed to keep peace in the region, called to establish a DMZ on the island for the possibility of negotiations. The statesman of Krodtzen reached out to Koranvistan for military support, in the event fighting should resume. The ceasefire and DMZ did not hold, and through joint operations, the Krodtzen and Yalokuts states asserted control over the region with the help of the Crown Military.

It was the Royal Guards first time in action, as well. Special Operations teams Vera and Gamma worked to remove the Black State Head and force final negotiations. The State of Vasiliy surrendered on April 29th, and the Trilateral Commission was formed to find a solution to Cieskahlias discord. The region would be incorporated into the Empire as a semi-autonomous republic, subject to the Empires laws, tax structures, and authority. However, Cieskahlia would also enjoy the benefits of connection to the greater network that Koranvistan enjoys.

And as of May 11th, the Empire began construction of 5 new Ferry stations, two airports, and a progressive overhaul of the Wireless Services infrastructure. And, in the Yalokuts area, a new railway was built out of the nation, through unmanaged territory and east towards the Empire of Corzerran.[/spoiler]

She chuckled, [i]"Overworking is Stani culture, my love. No need to worry. And she only had good things to say, but I'll be up front and say that you make a lot more sense now."[/i]

Cecilia gasped, asking to know more, and Elena took her hand while they walked from the kitchen with their drinks towards the gathered guests. [i]"Oh, you know the million strange habits a girl picks up along the way. I've noticed, and now I know where it comes from"[/i] she laughed and gave her partner a kiss, before entering the room and sitting down.

The group chatted late into the night and rose just as late to prepare for a feast that evening, as well as the first night of the Velnaz festival. It was a city-wide celebration, filled with local folk performances, art stalls, fireworks, and much more. Citizens wore traditional festival clothes, with brilliant floral and geometric patterns to their dresses and coats. Elena went out in a multicolored dress, with blue, green, white, and yellow patterns. Over this she wore her trenchcoat, and she spent most of the evening by Cecilia's side and around the King.
